anomalies.observed: The fan-tach input protection network on the Microcontroller sheet uses two plain diodes D3 and D4 in series with the FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH signals, in addition to the TVS diodes D5/D6.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes the fan-tach inputs as 'TVS-diode-protected inputs' and only identifies D5/D6 as the D_TVS devices; a series plain diode in the tach path is not part of the intended protection scheme and can prevent the MCU from correctly sensing the fan's open-drain low state.

evidence.quote: Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs, and raises a run fault if a fan stalls.
Microcontroller sheet: D3 and D4 are drawn as ordinary Device:D symbols in the FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH paths, while D5 and D6 are drawn as D_TVS symbols to GND.

anomalies.impact: If the series diodes are oriented to block the fan's pull-down, the ESP32 will not see the tach pulses and will falsely report a fan stall; if oriented the other way they add an unnecessary diode drop and degrade the tach signal.

parsed.summary: The design is largely consistent with the specification, but the fan-tach input network contains two plain series diodes (D3/D4) in addition to the specified TVS devices, which is not part of the intended TVS-only protection and could corrupt fan-stall sensing.
